name: Two horizons
symptom: floor lines and counter/shelf lines vanish to points at different heights; the room feels subtly 'off'
cause: the generator builds each surface locally; no single camera height (locally consistent, globally inconsistent)
detection_method: extend >= 3 receding horizontals per ground-parallel family; their VPs must lie on one horizontal line
fix: regenerate with fewer receding planes and an explicit camera ('eye-level camera at 1.6 m, level'); or crop out the offending object; or warp it to the main grid
evidence_label: EVIDENCE (projective geometry; observed in 25/25 DALL-E 2 kitchens)

name: Object off the room's grid
symptom: a box, counter or display case aligned with the walls converges to its own VPs, not the room's
cause: local object generation without shared vanishing structure
detection_method: extend the object's edges and the wall/floor edges; aligned objects must share VPs, rotated ones need VPs on the same horizon
fix: rotate/warp the object to the room VPs in post; or prompt the object 'parallel to the back wall'

name: Ground-parallel lines vanishing off the horizon
symptom: a flat tabletop or road converges to a point above or below the eye level
cause: inclined-plane logic used for a level surface, or a second camera height
detection_method: find the horizon from the floor; any level surface must vanish on it
fix: correct with a perspective warp; regenerate stating 'level table, horizon at ... height'

name: Slope vanishing on the horizon
symptom: a street that climbs or stairs that rise still vanish exactly on the horizon line
cause: the generator ignores that inclined planes have their own VP above (uphill) or below (downhill) the level VP
detection_method: uphill parallels must meet on a vertical above the level VP; downhill below
fix: repaint the slope lines to an auxiliary VP; or avoid slopes in AI backgrounds

name: Heads-on-horizon violation
symptom: on flat ground, equal-height people at different depths are cut by the horizon at different body heights (one at the eyes, another at the knees); some look like giants or dolls
cause: figures pasted/generated at sizes inconsistent with one camera height
detection_method: for each figure r = (feet->horizon)/(feet->head); equal-height figures must give equal r; camera at standing eye height -> all adult eyes on the horizon; Norling transfer line through feet and heads
fix: rescale/move figures to match r; or justify (stairs, stage, child, seated)

name: Mixed vertical convergence
symptom: some verticals are parallel, others lean toward a third VP
cause: the camera pitch is not consistent across the image
detection_method: extend 4+ verticals across the frame: all parallel (level camera) or all meeting at one VP3
fix: keystone-correct to parallel (shift-lens look) or regenerate with 'level camera, straight vertical lines'

name: Third vanishing point on the wrong side
symptom: a scene seen from above has verticals spreading downward (or a low-angle scene converging downward)
cause: pitch direction and convergence disagree
detection_method: looking down -> verticals meet below the frame; looking up -> above
fix: regenerate; mirror-correct is not possible

name: Warped boxes (vanishing points too close)
symptom: boxes and rooms look stretched, corners sharper than 90 deg, squares become diamonds
cause: station point too close / cone of vision exceeded; extreme wide-angle look
detection_method: estimate VP1-VP2 spacing; less than ~1.7x the image width means the view exceeds a 60-deg cone (DERIVED from Thales circle)
fix: move VPs off-canvas; ask for a longer lens look ('50 mm, distant viewpoint')

name: Unintended reverse perspective
symptom: a table top or box gets wider toward the back; side edges diverge
cause: the model mixes front and top views or copies naive/icon conventions
detection_method: extend the side edges: they must converge behind the object, not in front
fix: redraw the far edge shorter; regenerate with 'seen from the front, edges converge away from camera'

name: Isometric object in a perspective scene
symptom: one object keeps parallel edges (no convergence) while the room converges
cause: icon/infographic style leaking into a photo prompt or a pasted asset
detection_method: edges of the object stay parallel while comparable room edges converge
fix: re-render the object in perspective, or make the whole image isometric on purpose

name: Inconsistent floor/tile grid
symptom: tiles do not shrink regularly with distance; diagonals of tiles wander; grout lines curve
cause: texture painted, not projected
detection_method: draw the diagonals of several tiles: they must meet at one diagonal VP on the horizon; spacing must shrink smoothly
fix: replace the floor with a projected texture or a plain floor

name: Ellipse axis not aligned with the object's axis
symptom: a cup, wheel or lens rim looks twisted; the oval leans against its cylinder
cause: ellipses drawn by shape memory instead of from the axis
detection_method: the minor axis must lie along the cylinder's/lens's axis; the major axis perpendicular to it (T-shape)
fix: redraw ellipses on the minor axis; for glasses align both lens ellipses with the frame's facing direction

name: Wrong ellipse degree
symptom: circles far above or below the eye level are as flat as circles near it (or the reverse)
cause: degree not tied to distance from the horizon
detection_method: horizontal circles must get rounder the farther they are from the horizon; a circle on the horizon is a line
fix: redraw degrees in sequence (stacked plates, glasses in a display tray)

name: Centre placed at the ellipse's middle
symptom: a stem, screw or pin sits at the geometric centre of a receding circle and looks to float forward
cause: the perspective centre of a circle lies behind the ellipse's geometric centre
detection_method: draw the square around the circle in perspective and its diagonals; the crossing is the true centre
fix: move the stem slightly back along the minor axis

name: Mismatched lens pair (eyewear)
symptom: the two lenses of one frame differ in shape, size or ellipse orientation beyond what foreshortening explains
cause: the model treats each lens independently; symmetric product geometry is hard for generators
detection_method: mirror one lens over the bridge centre line (frontal) or check both ellipses share the minor-axis direction (3/4)
fix: composite the real cutout from the kit (Codex -i reference); never ship a generated frame as the product
evidence_label: DERIVED (from ellipse geometry and our product-accuracy rule)

name: Lens reflections that disagree
symptom: the left lens reflects a window, the right a different scene or light; highlights at inconsistent positions
cause: reflections synthesised per region; reflections are rare/ill-constrained in training data
detection_method: both lenses must mirror the same environment from nearly the same viewpoint; highlights consistent with the key light
fix: paint matching reflections or remove them (AR-coated look); light with one large soft source
evidence_label: DERIVED from reflection geometry; EVIDENCE that generators fail reflections

name: Shadows from different suns
symptom: cast shadows point in different directions or have different lengths for objects of similar height
cause: each object's shadow generated locally
detection_method: connect object points to their shadow points; all lines must meet at one point (the light's projection); shadows of parallel verticals converge to one shadow VP on the horizon
fix: repaint shadows to one light; or choose an overcast look (soft shadows) where errors are less visible

name: Floating object (no contact shadow)
symptom: glasses, feet or a product seem to hover above the surface
cause: missing occlusion shadow where object and surface meet; common in composites
detection_method: zoom to every contact point: there must be a dark, tight shadow
fix: add a contact shadow (multiply layer, soft, darkest at contact)
evidence_label: CRAFT + EVIDENCE (contact shadows anchor objects; see DRAWING_TECHNIQUES §5)

name: Impossible mirror/water reflection
symptom: reflection shifted, wrong size, or showing the object from an impossible angle
cause: reflection generated as a separate image
detection_method: vertical mirror: object->reflection lines converge to one point; water: reflection hangs from the point directly below the object, as far below as the object is above
fix: rebuild the reflection by flipping the object about the surface; or crop the mirror out

name: Wrong real-world scale
symptom: a pair of glasses as wide as a shoulder, a door shorter than a person, a counter at knee height
cause: the generator has no metric model; forced-perspective ambiguity
detection_method: compare with known sizes (door ~2 m, counter ~0.9-1 m, glasses front ~13-15 cm) via the horizon ratio
fix: rescale in post; mention sizes in the prompt ('glasses on a 90 cm counter')
evidence_label: DERIVED (typical sizes; verify with the kit's real frame)

name: Stretched edge objects
symptom: faces, lenses or balls near the frame edge of a wide image look egg-shaped
cause: correct wide-angle central projection seen from the wrong viewing distance
detection_method: compare round objects at the edge vs centre
fix: move key round objects toward the centre; describe a longer lens; or re-project (stereographic/Panini) for wide scenes

name: Unintended close-camera face
symptom: big nose, small ears, frame front oversized relative to temples - looks like an arm's-length selfie
cause: camera distance under ~1 m (often implied by '24 mm', 'selfie', 'close-up' prompts)
detection_method: nose-to-face-width ratio vs a reference; temples shrinking abruptly
fix: prompt 'photographed from 2 m with an 85 mm lens'; crop a wider frame instead of moving closer

name: Inverted atmospheric perspective
symptom: distant hills or buildings darker, sharper and more saturated than the middle ground
cause: uniform contrast or a pasted background
detection_method: compare contrast/saturation by depth band: it should drop with distance (daylight, haze)
fix: lift values and lower contrast/saturation of far planes; add haze

name: Blur not consistent with depth
symptom: objects at the same distance blurred differently, or a sharp far object next to a blurred near one at the same depth; tilt-shift band ignoring the ground plane
cause: blur applied as a layer effect, not from a focus plane
detection_method: map relative depths; blur must grow smoothly with distance from one focus plane (or follow a tilted plane)
fix: redo blur in post from a depth map (tools/depth.py) or ask for 'deep focus'

name: Partial fisheye
symptom: background lines curve but the product or a building stays rectilinear; lines through the centre curve
cause: style word 'fisheye' applied unevenly
detection_method: in a true fisheye, lines through the image centre stay straight and all others curve consistently with distance from the centre
fix: use a real fisheye remap in post or drop the effect

name: Camera angle not obeyed
symptom: asked for low angle or bird's eye, received a flat eye-level view with the horizon mid-frame
cause: text-to-image models are poorly trained for camera control and default to flat eye-level views
detection_method: check where the horizon is and whether verticals converge as expected for the requested pitch
fix: state the angle with height and direction ('camera at knee height tilted up 30 degrees'), add a visible cue (ceiling, sky, floor), use an image reference, or composite
